sentences.text: Cimoliasaurus grew to a length of 4 to 7 meters. Its name means "white chalk lizard" because the fossil deposits resemble the chalk of the Western Interior Seaway.
Fossils of Cimoliasaurus have been found in New Jersey, North Carolina, and Maryland.
A tentative record exists from Maryland, where a vertebra was discovered by Colin McEwen in 1988.
Cimoliasaurus is classified as a derived elasmosaurid, making the family Cimoliasauridae a junior synonym of Elasmosauridae.
The species Cimoliasaurus teplicensis is considered a nomen dubium.
Cimoliasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) in the eastern United States. The genus has a time range from the Kimmeridgian to the Maastrichtian (154.8 to 66 million years ago).
